scope: Release audit of the original-study explanations shown before a finding-page prediction. This audit does not reassess the original-to-later link or the later study outcome.

audit_stages.scope: The first 105 accepted records plus eight records each from source-review batches 11 and 12.
audit_stages.method: Programmatic schema, field-support, source-URL, aim-only-claim, and later-outcome screens covered all 121 records. The auditor read the supplied primary-source evidence for all 16 incoming records and six risk-selected accepted records; this was not a fresh full-source reread of all 105 earlier records.
audit_stages.initial_findings: One accepted record needed direct result evidence and all eight batch-11 records used aim or procedure language instead of an observed result.
audit_stages.resolution: The accepted record and all eight batch-11 records were repaired against their primary sources before inclusion in the current canonical file; all eight batch-12 records passed.

audit_stages.scope: Every accepted record from source-review batches 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, and 21.
audit_stages.method: The independent reader checked every display field and evidence entry against the supplied primary source or retained capture, as well as source identity and later-outcome leakage.
audit_stages.initial_findings: Twenty-nine records passed and six needed citation-completeness repairs; no false or unsupported original result, source-identity failure, or later-outcome leak was found.
audit_stages.resolution: All six citation-completeness repairs were applied to the canonical file.

audit_stages.method: Checked all four display-field support unions and all 31 cited excerpts against four retained Nature captures plus official Europe PMC and Wiley full text.

limits: A source-reviewed original explanation is not a certification that its linked later paper is a valid replication of the same effect, study, sample, or outcome.
The initial independent audit used complete programmatic screening plus risk-selected source rereading; it did not independently reread every one of the first 105 primary sources.
The 69 held records are preserved review work, not displayable explanations, and remain excluded until their stated source problem is resolved.
Only 156 of 4,626 finding records have this canonical four-field source-review tier; lower context tiers remain labeled separately.
